competency_fulfillment.rationale: None of the eighteen samples orders two or more similar (same-denominator) fractions; instead the set mixes single-fraction identification from shaded models (seed 43: 'A shape is divided into 4 equal parts. 3 parts are shaded.') with whole-number sorting (seed 44's 'Arrange these numbers from smallest to largest: 495, 231, 502').

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: The core skill of the competency, ordering similar fractions, is entirely absent; nine of the eighteen samples (seeds 44, 45, 50, 500, 501, 502, 600, 602, 609) order plain integers with no fraction involved at all.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: The integer-ordering items reach values like 834 and 510 (seed 44's '502', seed 600's '510'), a scale that has nothing to do with the similar-fraction concept this node should be teaching.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: There is no item type showing two or more like-denominator fractions (e.g. 2/5 and 4/5) placed in order; the fraction items that exist (seed 42, 46, 72: '2/5'; seed 603: '4/5') are each single-fraction reads of a model, not comparisons.

competency_alignment.rationale: The nine whole-number-ordering samples in this node are word-for-word identical to the same-seed samples in the sibling node mat_g2_na_q4_2 (e.g. seed 44's 'Arrange these numbers from smallest to largest: 495, 231, 502' appears in both), so this node is not producing content distinct to 'similar fractions' at all.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: The fraction values that are shown (2/5, 3/4, 2/4, 4/5) are all same-denominator ('similar') fractions consistent with the competency's stated fraction type, even though they are never placed in an ordering task.
